methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center study with 293 patients screened but only 13 (4.4%) TMB-high and 6 receiving pembrolizumab. Appropriate statistical tests (Fisher's exact, Mann-Whitney U, Kaplan-Meier, log-rank test) with p-values reported. Significant limitations: small treatment cohort (n=6) limiting power; heterogeneous prior treatments and varying PS at pembrolizumab initiation; no control group; selection bias from single specialized cancer center with potentially enriched genetic backgrounds.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Case series with direct clinical applicability to treatment selection. Describes pembrolizumab response in rare TMB-high pancreatic cancer subset with objective response rate (33.3%) and disease control (66.7%). High relevance for identifying and treating TMB-high cases, though single-center design and small n limits external generalizability.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods section adequately details patient selection, CGP testing platforms, molecular tumor board review, and statistical analysis with appropriate software cited. Genomic characteristics well-characterized with mutation frequencies and case tables. However, REMARK adherence incomplete: biomarker validation/verification procedures not fully detailed; no explicit data sharing statement regarding genomic data or clinical outcomes archival.

novelty_literature.justification: First to document pembrolizumab response in TMB-high pancreatic cancer with treatment efficacy data; prior studies (Quintanilha, Sakaida) reported frequency and genomic characteristics without treatment outcomes. Extends knowledge by showing MSI-H+TMB-high achieves better PFS (227 days) than MSS+TMB-high (90 days), identifying potential biomarker combination. Meaningful but incremental contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized Methods, Results, and Discussion sections clearly present patient cohort, genomic findings, and clinical outcomes. Figures effectively communicate mutation frequency distribution and Kaplan-Meier PFS curves. Discussion appropriately acknowledges limitations including small sample size, single-center design, and need for prospective validation.

key_strengths: First study documenting pembrolizumab efficacy in TMB-high pancreatic cancer with differential response by MSI-H status
Comprehensive genomic profiling with multiple CGP platforms (F1CDx, NCC Oncopanel, F1L) and expert molecular tumor board review
Clear identification of MSI-H+TMB-high subset with favorable response (67% disease control, 227-day median PFS) vs. MSS+TMB-high (33% disease control, 90-day median PFS)
key_concerns: Very small treatment sample (n=6 pembrolizumab-treated) severely limits statistical power and generalizability
Single-center referral hospital design potentially enriches for genetic backgrounds; authors acknowledge higher TMB-high rate (4.4%) than prior reports (1-2%)
Heterogeneous prior treatment regimens and performance status at pembrolizumab initiation without adjustment; no control group or comparative cohort
Threshold validity for TMB≥10 mut/Mb not validated in pancreatic cancer; manuscript notes Case 8 with TMB>50 had disease progression
chief_reviewer.rationale: Clinically important case series describing rare TMB-high pancreatic cancer treated with pembrolizumab, with emerging evidence for MSI-H+TMB-high as predictive marker. Limited by small sample and single-center design; major revisions needed to expand cohort, validate biomarker thresholds, and clarify data sharing.
